title: Tenanted traffic fencing and compatibility probes for staged model variants
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Current staged rollouts expose variants broadly to traffic slices that span multiple tenants and capacity tiers. We lack a lightweight, tenant-aware fencing mechanism combined with fine-grained compatibility probes to decide safe ramping. That increases blast radius and unnecessary rollbacks in noisy, multi-tenant workloads.

Goal: Implement a tenant-aware traffic fencing layer (safety lanes) that confines early canaries and shadow experiments to narrow tenant cohorts and capacity tiers while running compatibility probes (semantic, latency, and token-cost checks). Integrate probe signals into the rollout controller so region failovers, tier spillovers, and automatic rollback triggers are driven by a combined compatibility score and capacity-aware heuristics.

This ticket covers: design + runtime changes to routing, probe definition and scoring, rollout controller integration, observability (per-tenant metrics), and automated rollback thresholds. It does NOT include multi-cloud mesh wiring or UI in Console; those are follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Safety-lane API: allow defining tenant cohorts + capacity-tier constraints for staged traffic
Compatibility probes: runtime can run per-request lightweight probes that return pass/warn/fail with score
Rollout controller consumes probe scores and tenant-level SLOs to alter ramp rates and trigger rollback
Region failovers honor tenant fencing and do not move tenant traffic into incompatible model variants
End-to-end test harness that simulates 100 tenants across 3 capacity tiers and evaluates behavioural correctness
Documentation: developer-facing guide describing how to configure tenant fences and probe definitions
notes: Trade-offs considered: embedding probes into every request increases tail latency but gives higher-fidelity signals; chosen approach is sampled probes with cached probe state per-tenant to limit cost.
We will prioritize 'low-volume, high-sensitivity' tenants for initial gates (legal/compliance customers).
Backwards compatibility: default safety-lane is empty so existing rollouts remain unchanged until configured.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature flag behind runtime + controller flags, internal test tenants only
Phase 1: enable safety-lane for 10 internal tenants and run synthetic probes for 48h
Phase 2: extend to 50 customers + enable automatic rollback at score < 0.6 for 5m window
Phase 3: public release with templates for common tenant cohorts and Console integrations
test_plan: Unit: probe scoring library + routing matcher
Integration: end-to-end simulation (simulated tenants, spike failure scenarios, region outage): assert correct spillback and no cross-tenant contamination
Performance: measure added 95th tail latency for safety-lane checks under 5% baseline
Chaos: memory pressure + kernel slowdowns to validate degraded fallback behaviour
metrics: rollbacks triggered by probe-score vs by capacity loss
risk_mitigation: Sampling probes rather than probing every request to bound cost and latency impact
Grace period in rollout controller: require sustained failure for 5m before auto-rollback
Circuit-breaker: if tier capacity falls below 30% use conservative spillback policy
Manual override: ops can force traffic fencing toggle per-tenant via control-plane API
